ask: We're an agency. Acme wants to sign off every post before it goes out. Set that up and get next week's 4 drafts to them.

steps.why: Acme's row gives the brand's clock and review mode. It does not show whether client sign-off is required, so that is read from a post next.
Next week's 4 drafts, numbered with account and full text, so the user sees exactly what the client will see. Rows don't say whether a post is already with the client.
client_signoff.required tells whether the brand already requires sign-off; state says not_sent, waiting_on_client or signed_off. Here required is false: the switch is off.
Who is on the team. Client reviewers are never listed, so the user is asked who at Acme signs off. Missing on this app: ask by name.

say: Here's how I'd set it up for Acme. Every post must have their yes: that's the "Client sign-off required" switch in Acme's settings, Approvals section. Only your organization owner can turn it on, and it pulls any scheduled post without a client yes back to waiting, so turn it on before scheduling. Invite Acme's approver as a client reviewer in People & access (no seat). Mark someone required only if their own yes is a must. Then send these 4 drafts from Approvals: bolta.ai/dashboard/approvals. They get reminders on days 2 and 5. Don't move a time after sending: the client saw it, and a new one means sending again. I'll check where each post stands whenever you ask.
never: Saying the drafts were sent to the client: a hand-picked request is sent in Bolta, not from here.
Approving the drafts for the team to save the client a step.
Telling a creator they can approve any post for the team: a creator approves only Bolta's drafts and posts naming them reviewer, and a refusal names the role.
Moving a post's time while the client hasn't answered without saying it voids the request.
